steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Campaigns aim to achieve specific changes in policy, behaviour, or awareness. Successful campaigns have clear messages, identifiable targets, and measurable goals.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Campaign methods include: petitions, marches and demonstrations, social media campaigns, lobbying elected representatives, public meetings, letter-writing, boycotts, and civil disobedience.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Advocacy means representing and arguing for the rights and interests of others, especially those who may not be able to represent themselves effectively.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Grassroots campaigns are built from the community level up (e.g. local residents opposing a development). Top-down campaigns are led by established organisations (e.g. Oxfam, Amnesty International).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between campaigning and advocacy? | Q: Give two examples of effective campaigns and explain why they succeeded. | Q: What role does social media play in modern campaigning?
